name: Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA)
evidence_rating: early and thin: authorisation counts measured; two small quasi-experimental studies on stablecoin markets; nothing on fraud, consumer losses or funding
summary: MiCA set up EU licences for crypto firms and stablecoin issuers. By October 2026 about 365 firms were licensed and licensed euro stablecoins had more than doubled in value to about USD 674 million, though from a tiny base. Early studies find MiCA moved EU exchanges from unlicensed to licensed stablecoins but barely changed wider markets; promised savings on remittances and reductions in fraud have not been measured.

indicators.objective: Remove regulatory obstacles to issuance, trading and post-trading of crypto-assets; increase company funding through ICOs/STOs; limit fraud and illicit practices; give consumers and investors access to new investment and payment instruments

indicators.indicator: Number of entities authorised in the EU as crypto-asset service providers
indicators.evidence: Measured: ESMA interim register (downloaded 10 Oct 2026) lists 370 authorised CASP entries (365 distinct legal entities) across 27 EU/EEA states, 103 of them in Germany; authorisations peaked around the end of the transitional period (30 June 2026). A separate list names 173 non-compliant entities.

indicators.indicator: Number of authorised issuers of asset-referenced / significant tokens; market capitalisation of such tokens
indicators.evidence: ESMA register: zero authorised asset-referenced token issuers; 25 e-money token issuers with 50 white papers. Industry tracker: market cap of eight MiCA-compliant euro stablecoins rose from USD 296m to USD 674m (June 2025-June 2026), still tiny against dollar stablecoins.

indicators.indicator: Number and value of fraud and thefts of crypto-assets in the EU; market abuse cases reported and investigated
indicators.evidence: Not measured: no EU-level statistics published. Commission's Article 140 report on application (interim due 30 June 2025) not located on EUR-Lex; public consultation opened May 2026.

indicators.indicator: Number and volumes of crypto-asset issuances in the EU
indicators.evidence: White papers for other crypto-assets are notified to ESMA's register, but no volume statistics or analysis of company funding found.

indicators.indicator: Remittance cost savings EUR 220-570m a year; crypto funding costs 20-40% below IPOs
indicators.evidence: Not measured. ESMA (2024): euro plays a minor role in crypto trading and MiCA's announcement did not raise euro transactions.

indicators.indicator: One-off EUR 2.8-16.5m and ongoing EUR 2.2-24m for newly regulated CASPs; about EUR 35,000 per SME issuance

literature.citation: European Commission (2020), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Regulation on Markets in Crypto-assets (executive summary SWD(2020) 381), SWD(2020) 380
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal for a Regulation on Markets in Crypto-assets (executive summary SWD(2020) 381)
literature.outcomes: remittance costs; funding costs; compliance costs
literature.headline: Remittance cost savings EUR 220-570m a year; crypto-asset funding costs 20-40% lower than IPOs of similar size; one-off compliance costs EUR 2.8-16.5m and ongoing EUR 2.2-24m for newly regulated service providers; about EUR 35,000 per SME issuance
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected MiCA to save EUR 220-570 million a year on remittances and give start-ups cheaper funding than stock-market listings, at modest compliance cost.

literature.citation: ESMA (2026), Interim MiCA register (authorised CASPs, e-money token issuers, ART issuers, non-compliant entities), ESMA CSV files, accessed 10 Oct 2026
literature.title: Interim MiCA register (authorised CASPs, e-money token issuers, ART issuers, non-compliant entities)
literature.headline: 370 authorised CASP entries (365 entities) in 27 EU/EEA states (Germany 103, France 36, Netherlands 29); 25 e-money token issuers; no asset-referenced token issuers; 173 entities flagged as non-compliant
literature.summary_plain: By October 2026, about 365 crypto firms had a MiCA licence, more than a quarter of them in Germany, while no one had been authorised to issue an asset-backed 'stablecoin' basket.

literature.citation: Calissano, Giuglini & Reiche (ESMA) (2024), Crypto-assets: Market structures and EU relevance, ESMA TRV Risk Analysis, 10 April 2024
literature.title: Crypto-assets: Market structures and EU relevance
literature.headline: Only 20-30% of transactions involve fiat; euro plays a minor role and MiCA's announcement has not raised euro transactions; ten exchanges process about 90% of trades; about 55% of volume on exchanges holding an EU VASP licence, though most likely occurs outside the EU
literature.summary_plain: Before MiCA applied, ESMA found the euro played only a minor role in crypto trading and the new law's announcement had not changed that.

literature.citation: Borri & Shakhnov (2026), Does Regulation Bite at Gateways? Evidence from MiCA and Stablecoins, arXiv 2607.09514
literature.title: Does Regulation Bite at Gateways? Evidence from MiCA and Stablecoins
literature.method: event study / treated-vs-control comparison of 14 exchanges (EEA-facing vs global), daily 2024-2025
literature.headline: Aggregate stablecoin market shares and volumes barely move after MiCA-driven USDT delistings; on EEA-facing exchanges USDC share rises by 0.82 and relative volume by 0.54 pre-event standard deviations as USDT trading contracts
literature.summary_plain: MiCA pushed EU-facing exchanges from the unlicensed USDT stablecoin to the licensed USDC, but barely changed the global market.

literature.citation: Fauche (2025), The impact of MiCAR on the stablecoin market (summary of master's thesis), Financial Forum / Bank- en Financiewezen, 10 Dec 2025
literature.title: The impact of MiCAR on the stablecoin market (summary of master's thesis)
literature.venue: Financial Forum / Bank- en Financiewezen, 10 Dec 2025
literature.method: event study (5 euro stablecoins) and difference-in-differences vs non-EU stablecoins, around EP approval 20 April 2023
literature.headline: No significant effect of MiCAR approval on returns, volatility or trading volume overall; positive return response for the three largest euro stablecoins
literature.summary_plain: A student study found MiCA's approval had no measurable effect on euro stablecoins' prices or trading, apart from a small positive reaction for the largest coins.
literature.quality: short window; small sample; not peer reviewed

literature.citation: Decta (2026), Euro Stablecoin Trends Report 2026: The MiCA-Compliant Coins in the EU Market, Decta (payments company) report
literature.title: Euro Stablecoin Trends Report 2026: The MiCA-Compliant Coins in the EU Market
literature.outcomes: euro stablecoin market cap and volume
literature.headline: Market cap of eight MiCA-compliant euro stablecoins rose 128% from USD 295.6m to USD 673.9m (June 2025-June 2026); average daily trading volume up 43%
literature.summary_plain: Licensed euro stablecoins more than doubled in value over the year after MiCA, though from a very small base.

literature.authors: Thomas Conlon, Shaen Corbet, Les Oxley
literature.title: The influence of European MiCa regulation on cryptocurrencies
literature.method: event study of crypto-asset returns around MiCA-related announcements
literature.headline: Announcement-day returns fell by about 2.1% around MiCA announcements, persisting up to three days, with stronger effects for digital assets, platform tokens and utility tokens.
literature.summary_plain: Crypto prices dipped by about 2% on days when news about the EU's MiCA rules came out, especially for some token types.
literature.period_geography: MiCA legislative milestones (approx. 2020-2023); global crypto markets
literature.quality: Standard event study of announcements (legislative stage, not application); headline taken from the search-engine abstract snippet, publisher page blocked, metadata confirmed via Crossref/Unpaywall.
literature.citation: Thomas Conlon, Shaen Corbet, Les Oxley (2024), The influence of European MiCa regulation on cryptocurrencies, Global Finance Journal 63 (2024), doi:10.1016/j.gfj.2024.101040

literature.title: MiCA: The end of the transitional period for CASPs - What comes after 1 July 2026?
literature.method: descriptive tabulation of the ESMA interim MiCA register
literature.outcomes: number and location of authorised CASPs
literature.headline: As of June 2026 about 216 firms had MiCA authorisation versus more than 1,200 crypto service providers previously registered under national AML regimes, concentrated in Germany (55), the Netherlands (26) and France (19).
literature.summary_plain: A consultancy counted how many crypto firms had obtained the new EU licence just before the transition period ended. Only about one in six of the previously registered firms had done so, mostly in a few countries.
literature.quality: Simple descriptive counts from official register; marketing piece for Cyprus
literature.citation: KPMG Cyprus (2026), MiCA: The end of the transitional period for CASPs - What comes after 1 July 2026?, KPMG Limited (Cyprus) briefing

literature.title: Kaiko/Bitvavo report on crypto trading in Europe (MiCA-compliant stablecoins dominate European market)
literature.method: descriptive analysis of exchange trading data
literature.outcomes: euro crypto trading volumes; euro stablecoin market shares and volumes
literature.headline: After MiCA's stablecoin rules applied (June 2024), MiCA-compliant coins captured most of the euro-stablecoin market, while monthly euro-stablecoin volumes exceeded $300 million through 2024 (peak near $800 million in November) and Tether discontinued EURT.
literature.summary_plain: A crypto data firm found that once MiCA rules began, euro stablecoins that met the rules took over most of their market as exchanges dropped non-compliant coins.
literature.quality: Descriptive industry data; no counterfactual; primary report not accessible, figures from press coverage
literature.interested_party: Bitvavo is a crypto exchange subject to MiCA; Kaiko sells market data
literature.citation: Kaiko Research & Bitvavo (2024), Kaiko/Bitvavo report on crypto trading in Europe (MiCA-compliant stablecoins dominate European market), Kaiko Research (reported by Cointelegraph, 18 Dec 2024)

literature.authors: Bindseil, U. & Voloder, E. (Blockchain for Europe)
literature.title: Reforming MiCA for Euro Stablecoins
literature.method: structured qualitative assessment of MiCA e-money-token rules with market data (DeFiLlama) and international comparison
literature.outcomes: euro stablecoin competitiveness, reserve rules, remuneration ban
literature.headline: The report argues MiCA has made euro stablecoins safe but commercially weak, citing data that euro stablecoins remain under 1% of global stablecoin volume against a dollar-stablecoin market above $300 billion.
literature.summary_plain: A crypto industry group, with a former ECB official, argues that MiCA's strict rules on reserves and the ban on paying interest have kept euro stablecoins tiny next to dollar ones.
literature.quality: Advocacy-oriented assessment with light descriptive data; no causal analysis
literature.interested_party: Industry association of blockchain firms lobbying for MiCA reform
literature.citation: Bindseil, U. & Voloder, E. (Blockchain for Europe) (2026), Reforming MiCA for Euro Stablecoins, Blockchain for Europe joint report
